experiences.name: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the medieval cobblestone streets of Staré Město, witness the iconic Orloj Astronomical Clock strike the hour with its parade of apostles, and explore the Gothic Týn Church. Join a free walking tour to uncover centuries of Bohemian history, legends, and architecture without breaking the budget.

experiences.name: Budapest Ruin Bar Crawl & Local Street Food Night
experiences.description: Dive into Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene starting at Szimpla Kert, the original ruin pub set in a crumbling pre-war building. Graze on local street food including lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) and kürtőskalács (chimney cake) from nearby vendors. A quintessential Budapest cultural and culinary experience.

experiences.name: Buda Castle Hill & Fisherman's Bastion Exploration
experiences.description: Cross the iconic Chain Bridge and climb Castle Hill to explore the Royal Palace complex, Matthias Church, and the fairy-tale turrets of Fisherman's Bastion offering panoramic views over the Danube and Pest. Stroll through cobblestone lanes lined with baroque architecture and absorb over 1,000 years of Hungarian royal history.

experiences.name: Czech Culinary Experience: Traditional Lunch & Pilsner Tasting
experiences.description: Settle into a classic Prague pivnice (pub) in the Vinohrady neighborhood for a hearty Czech lunch featuring svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce with bread dumplings) or roast pork with sauerkraut. Pair it with a freshly tapped Pilsner Urquell or Kozel dark beer. Optionally join a short guided food tour of local markets for an extra cultural layer.

experiences.name: Széchenyi Thermal Bath Soak
experiences.description: Unwind in one of Europe's largest and most magnificent thermal bath complexes, a Budapest institution since 1913. Soak in the grand neo-baroque outdoor and indoor pools fed by natural hot springs reaching 77°C. A deeply local experience where Budapestians of all ages relax, play chess on floating boards, and socialize — the perfect cultural and restorative activity mid-trip.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Eastern Europe — Prague & Budapest
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30. Take the budget-friendly Airport Express bus (Line AE) or city bus 119 to the city center. Check in to your accommodation, drop off luggage, and take a short relaxing walk around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings. Grab a late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or 24-hour kebab shop.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Late-night street food or convenience store near accommodation — budget ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8)

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy low on arrival night. Have local Czech koruna (CZK) ready or use airport ATM. Avoid airport exchange kiosks — use a no-fee ATM instead. Prague uses CZK, not euros.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a slow breakfast then walk to Prague's Old Town Square (Staroměstské náměstí). Watch the famous Astronomical Clock (Orloj) chime on the hour. Explore the medieval square, Church of Our Lady before Týn, and surrounding Gothic architecture — all free to view from outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (free) and climb to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad) — the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Visit St. Vitus Cathedral (free entry to the nave), the Old Royal Palace, and enjoy panoramic views over the red rooftops of Prague. Budget tip: the castle grounds are free; only select interior buildings require a ticket (~250 CZK for the basic circuit).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back down through Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Enjoy the charming cobblestone streets and baroque architecture. Head to a local pub for a classic Czech dinner and the world's cheapest quality beer.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry (trdelník or rohlik) from a local bakery — budget ~50–80 CZK (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch menu (polední menu) at a local Czech restaurant near Old Town — soup + main course for ~150–200 CZK (~€6–8). Try svíčková (beef sirloin with cream sauce) or goulash with bread dumplings.
meals.dinner: Traditional Czech pub dinner — pork knee (vepřové koleno) or schnitzel with a half-liter of Pilsner Urquell or Kozel beer at a local pivnice (pub) — budget ~200–280 CZK (~€8–11)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Prague's cobblestones are beautiful but uneven. Public transport day pass costs ~120 CZK (~€5) and covers trams, metro, and buses. Validate your ticket before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jewish Quarter (Josefov) — walk through the historic streets and admire the Old Jewish Cemetery and synagogue exteriors. The full museum entry is ~500 CZK but exterior exploration is free. Then head to the nearby Municipal House (Obecní dům) for a look at its stunning Art Nouveau facade — free from outside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Vinohrady or Žižkov neighborhoods — authentic, less touristy areas loved by locals. Visit the quirky Žižkov Television Tower (exterior free, observation deck ~250 CZK) decorated with crawling baby sculptures by artist David Černý. Browse local markets or vintage shops. Visit Riegrovy sady park for city views and a beer garden with cold Czech lager at local prices.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a budget classical music or organ concert — Prague has many affordable evening performances in historic churches (~300–500 CZK). Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed evening in a local wine bar or craft beer pub in Vinohrady.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near accommodation — coffee + toast or eggs — budget ~100–150 CZK (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh open-faced sandwich (chlebíček) from a local deli or market — budget ~80–120 CZK (~€3–5)
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood restaurant in Žižkov or Vinohrady — hearty Czech or Eastern European meal — budget ~200–250 CZK (~€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: September in Prague is pleasant — mild temperatures around 15–20°C. Bring a light jacket for evenings. Avoid tourist-trap restaurants directly on Old Town Square — prices are 2–3x higher for the same food.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-18 (Friday) — Prague Day 3: Parks, Markets & Departure Prep
day_by_day.morning: Visit Letná Park (Letenské sady) for a beautiful morning walk and the best free panoramic view of Prague's bridges and river. Relax at the famous Letná beer garden with a morning coffee or early beer like a local. Then explore the nearby Stromovka Park — Prague's largest park, perfect for a peaceful stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Náplavka Farmers' Market along the Vltava riverbank (open Saturdays, but Friday has riverside activity too) or browse Palladium or Nový Smíchov for budget shopping. Visit the Dancing House (Tančící dům) — a famous deconstructivist building — free to admire from outside. Pack your bags and prepare for tomorrow's travel to Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Final Prague dinner — splurge slightly on a sit-down Czech restaurant. Try roast duck (pečená kachna) with red cabbage and potato dumplings. Take a final evening walk across Charles Bridge at dusk for magical golden-hour views.

meals.breakfast: Letná beer garden café — coffee and pastry — budget ~100 CZK (~€4)
meals.lunch: Street food near Náplavka — grilled sausage (klobása) with mustard and bread — budget ~80–100 CZK (~€3–4)
meals.dinner: Farewell Prague dinner at a mid-range local restaurant — budget ~300–350 CZK (~€12–14)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Prague–Budapest transport in advance for best budget prices. Options: FlixBus (~€15–25, ~7 hours), RegioJet train or bus (~€20–30), or budget airlines like Wizz Air/Ryanair (~€20–50 if booked early). Overnight bus is the most budget-friendly option.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-19 (Saturday) — Travel Day: Prague → Budapest + Arrival Exploration
day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure from Prague to Budapest (if taking daytime FlixBus or train — approximately 6–7 hours journey). Pack snacks from a local supermarket (Albert, Billa, or Lidl) to save money on the road. Enjoy the scenic countryside views through Czech Republic, Slovakia, and into Hungary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest. Check in to accommodation. Budapest uses Hungarian Forint (HUF) — use a local ATM upon arrival. Take a first walk along the Danube riverbank to soak in the stunning views of the Parliament Building and Buda Castle. Explore the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) — a stunning 19th-century iron market hall with local produce, spices, and street food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Walk across the iconic Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) at sunset for stunning views of both Buda and Pest sides. Explore the lively ruin bar district in the Jewish Quarter of Pest — grab a drink at the famous Szimpla Kert, Budapest's original ruin bar, which has a vibrant Saturday farmers' market atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from Prague supermarket for the journey — budget ~200 CZK (~€8)
meals.lunch: On the bus/train — packed food or stop at a service station
meals.dinner: First Hungarian meal at Great Market Hall upper floor — lángos (deep-fried dough with sour cream and cheese) or goulash soup — budget ~2,000–2,500 HUF (~€5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Budapest is divided into Buda (hilly, historic) and Pest (flat, urban). Most budget accommodation and nightlife is on the Pest side. Budapest public transport day pass costs ~2,500 HUF (~€6.50) — excellent value for metro, trams, and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Take the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló) or hike up Castle Hill to Buda Castle (Budavári Palota). Explore the free Castle District — Fisherman's Bastion (Halászbástya) offers fairy-tale towers and the best panoramic views of Pest and the Danube (free entry to the lower terraces; upper terraces ~700 HUF). Visit the stunning Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) — ~1,500 HUF entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down through the charming Castle Hill streets and cross over to Pest. Visit the Hungarian Parliament Building exterior — the most beautiful Neo-Gothic parliament in the world (guided tours available ~6,000 HUF but exterior is free and spectacular). Walk along the Danube Promenade and visit the deeply moving Shoes on the Danube Bank memorial — free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Gozsdu Udvar (Gozsdu Court) — a series of connected courtyards filled with restaurants, bars, and street food stalls in the heart of the Jewish Quarter. Try a chimney cake (kürtőskalács) from a street vendor.

meals.breakfast: Local café near accommodation — coffee and kifli (Hungarian crescent roll) — budget ~800–1,000 HUF (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Affordable Hungarian lunch menu near Castle Hill — goulash soup (gulyásleves) + main dish — budget ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9)
meals.dinner: Street food and snacks at Gozsdu Udvar — lángos, grilled meats, chimney cake — budget ~2,000–3,000 HUF (~€5–8)

day_by_day.notes: September is one of the best months to visit Budapest — warm days (~18–22°C), fewer crowds than summer, and golden autumn light perfect for photography. Comfortable shoes are essential for Castle Hill's cobblestones.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-21 (Monday) — Budapest Day 2: Thermal Baths, Markets & Local Life
day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Széchenyi Thermal Bath (Széchenyi Gyógyfürdő) — the largest thermal bath complex in Europe, housed in a stunning Neo-Baroque yellow palace in City Park. Budget entry with locker ~6,500–7,500 HUF (~€16–19). Soak in the outdoor pools and indoor thermal pools — a quintessential Budapest experience. Morning visits are less crowded.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through City Park (Városliget) — free and beautiful. Visit Vajdahunyad Castle (exterior free) — a romanticized replica of Transylvanian architecture. Head to the Hungarian State Opera House to admire the stunning exterior (budget guided tours available ~3,000 HUF). Stroll down Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand boulevard, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Quarter ruin bars for a classic Budapest evening. Visit Instant-Fogas complex or Ellátó Kert for affordable craft beers and local cocktails. Alternatively, take a budget night cruise on the Danube (~5,000–7,000 HUF) for illuminated views of the Parliament and bridges.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry from a local pékség (bakery) — pogácsa (savory scone) or rétes (strudel) — budget ~500–700 HUF (~€1.50–2)
meals.lunch: Affordable lunch at a local étterem (restaurant) — chicken paprikash (paprikás csirke) with nokedli dumplings — budget ~2,500–3,500 HUF (~€6–9)
meals.dinner: Ruin bar district — affordable bites and drinks — budget ~3,000–4,000 HUF (~€8–10) including drinks

day_by_day.notes: Bring a swimsuit and towel for the thermal baths (or rent towels on-site for ~1,000 HUF). Lockers are mandatory. The thermal baths are genuinely therapeutic and a must-do cultural experience in Budapest.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street (Dohány utcai zsinagóga) — the largest synagogue in Europe and second largest in the world (~4,000 HUF entry). The adjacent Holocaust Memorial Garden with its weeping willow tree is deeply moving. Explore the surrounding Jewish Quarter's street art, murals, and independent coffee shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Central Market Hall (Központi Vásárcsarnok) for last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, pálinka (fruit brandy), or embroidered textiles at local prices (far cheaper than tourist shops). Grab a final Hungarian lunch here. Take a last walk along the Danube and across Liberty Bridge (Szabadság híd) — free and one of the most beautiful bridges in Budapest.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Budapest dinner at a classic Hungarian restaurant. Try beef goulash (marhagulyás), stuffed peppers (töltött paprika), or Hortobágyi palacsinta (savory crepes with meat filling). Head to the airport or station for onward travel. Budapest Liszt Ferenc Airport is accessible by bus 100E (~900 HUF direct, ~30 min) — the most budget-friendly airport transfer.

meals.breakfast: Final Hungarian café breakfast — coffee, pastry, and fresh juice — budget ~1,000–1,500 HUF (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Central Market Hall upper floor — hearty Hungarian plate — budget ~2,500–3,000 HUF (~€6–8)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a local Hungarian restaurant — budget ~4,000–5,000 HUF (~€10–13)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some HUF for bus 100E to the airport (~900 HUF). Allow 2.5–3 hours before flight departure for airport check-in. Overall 8-day trip budget estimate: Prague ~€80–120 total (excl. accommodation & transport), Budapest ~€90–130 total. Both cities are among the most affordable capitals in Europe — excellent value for budget travelers.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Václav Havel Airport Prague at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to your hotel in Prague. Take the Airport Express bus or an Uber/taxi (~30 min, ~€15-20). Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light late-night snack near the hotel — try a 24-hour convenience store or a nearby kebab/street food stand if hunger strikes after check-in

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is late. Have local Czech koruna (CZK) or a card ready for the taxi. Prague is very safe at night.

day_by_day.morning: Start your Prague exploration with the iconic Prague Castle complex. Arrive early (~9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace, and the Golden Lane. Enjoy sweeping panoramic views of the red-roofed city from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through the charming Malá Strana (Lesser Town) neighborhood. Cross the famous Charles Bridge, admiring its Baroque statues and views of the Vltava River. Stroll into the Old Town (Staré Město) and visit the Old Town Square, watching the Astronomical Clock chime on the hour. Explore the nearby Jewish Quarter (Josefov) with its historic synagogues and cemetery.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening walk along the Vltava riverbank. Head to the Vinohrady or Old Town area for dinner at a traditional Czech restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café Savoy or a local bakery near the hotel — try a fresh croissant and coffee (~€5-8)
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — a beloved mid-range Czech pub serving classic svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce) and fresh Pilsner Urquell on tap (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Čestr Restaurant — quality Czech cuisine with dishes like roast duck and dumplings in a cozy setting (~€15-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Prague Castle entry tickets cost ~€12-15 for the full circuit. Wear comfortable walking shoes — cobblestone streets are everywhere. The Astronomical Clock chimes every hour on the hour.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Wenceslas Square and the surrounding New Town (Nové Město). Visit the National Museum at the top of the square (re-opened after renovation — stunning neo-Renaissance interior). Walk through the bustling Lucerna Passage, a beautiful Art Nouveau arcade with quirky artwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short metro or tram ride to Vinohrady and Žižkov neighborhoods — two of Prague's most authentic, less-touristy districts. Climb the Žižkov Television Tower (with its famous crawling baby sculptures) for panoramic city views. Wander the leafy streets and discover local cafés and bookshops.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a classical music concert or opera performance — Prague has world-class venues like the State Opera or Rudolfinum at very affordable prices (~€15-35). Alternatively, enjoy a relaxed evening beer at a local pivnice (pub) in Žižkov, one of Prague's most traditional beer-drinking neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Café Imperial — a stunning Art Deco café serving excellent breakfast buffet or à la carte (~€8-12)
meals.lunch: Manifesto Market (if open in September) — a trendy street food container market with diverse affordable options (~€6-10)
meals.dinner: Eska — a celebrated modern Czech bistro in Karlín district using local seasonal ingredients, great value (~€18-25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check opera/concert schedules at the National Theatre or State Opera in advance and book online. Žižkov has a gritty, authentic charm — embrace it!

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Kutná Hora (~1 hour by train from Prague's main station, trains run frequently). Visit the hauntingly beautiful Sedlec Ossuary (Bone Church) — a medieval chapel decorated with the bones of ~40,000 people. Then explore the stunning Gothic Cathedral of St. Barbara, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Prague by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon exploring the Letná Park area — walk up to Letná Beer Garden for a cold Czech beer and incredible views over the city and Vltava River. Nearby, visit the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art if you enjoy modern culture.
day_by_day.evening: It's Friday night — experience Prague's vibrant nightlife responsibly. Start with drinks at a rooftop bar (try T-Anker or Terasa U Zlaté studně for views), then enjoy dinner in the lively Dlouhá Street area.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel or grab a párek v rohlíku (Czech hot dog) from a street stand near the train station
meals.lunch: In Kutná Hora — try Restaurant Dačický, a historic tavern serving hearty Czech food at local prices (~€8-12)
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (splurge option) or Nase Maso — a beloved butcher-restaurant hybrid serving incredible burgers and Czech meats (~€12-16)

day_by_day.notes: Train to Kutná Hora costs ~€5-7 return. The Ossuary is a 10-min walk from Sedlec station or 20-min walk from Kutná Hora town station. Book tickets online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Prague to Budapest by train or FlixBus. The scenic train journey takes ~6.5-7 hours (depart ~8:00-9:00 AM, arrive early afternoon). Book in advance via Omio or RegioJet — comfortable seats, dining car available. Enjoy the Central European countryside passing by.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Budapest (Keleti or Kelenföld station). Check in to your Budapest accommodation. Take a gentle orientation walk along the Danube riverbank — admire the stunning Parliament Building from the Pest side. Walk across the iconic Chain Bridge for your first views of Buda Castle Hill.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome to Budapest! Head to the Great Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) if still open, or explore the lively Ráday Street food and restaurant strip for your first Hungarian dinner.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee at Prague's main train station before boarding
meals.lunch: Dining car on the train or packed snacks — enjoy the journey
meals.dinner: Menza Restaurant — a retro-chic Hungarian bistro in Budapest's Party District serving excellent gulyás and Hungarian classics (~€14-20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets at least a few days in advance — RegioJet offers comfortable, affordable Prague-Budapest trains with WiFi and seat service. Alternatively, Flixbus is cheaper but slower. The Keleti station is central and well-connected by metro.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Buda side of the city. Take the historic Funicular (or hike up) to Buda Castle Hill. Visit the Royal Palace (Hungarian National Gallery inside), Matthias Church, and the Fisherman's Bastion — offering some of Europe's most photogenic views over the Danube and Pest skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and cross to the Pest side. Visit the magnificent Hungarian Parliament Building (book a guided interior tour in advance — ~€12). Walk along the Grand Boulevard and explore the atmospheric Erzsébetváros (7th District / Jewish Quarter) — home to the Great Synagogue (Europe's largest) and the famous ruin bars.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's legendary ruin bar scene at Szimpla Kert — the original and most iconic ruin bar, set in a crumbling courtyard filled with eclectic decor, local craft beer, and live music. Perfect for a Sunday evening as Szimpla hosts its famous farmers' market on Sunday mornings too.

meals.breakfast: New York Café — a breathtakingly ornate historic café, perfect for a special Sunday breakfast (~€12-18, splurge-worthy)
meals.lunch: Hungarikum Bisztró — excellent traditional Hungarian food near the Parliament, try the gulyás soup and lángos (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Street food and snacks at Szimpla Kert ruin bar, or grab a kürtőskalács (chimney cake) from a street vendor (~€5-8 casual)

day_by_day.notes: Parliament tours must be booked in advance at the official website. Matthias Church charges a small entry fee (~€5). September evenings can be cool — bring a light jacket for the outdoor ruin bar.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in one of Budapest's legendary thermal bath experiences. Visit Széchenyi Thermal Bath in City Park — the largest medicinal bath in Europe, with stunning yellow neo-Baroque architecture. Soak in the outdoor and indoor pools rich with natural geothermal water. Arrive early to enjoy it before it gets busy (~9:00 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) surrounding the baths. Visit Vajdahunyad Castle — a fairy-tale castle built for the 1896 millennium exhibition. Stroll down Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's grand Champs-Élysées-style boulevard — stopping at the Hungarian State Opera House (exterior or guided tour). Visit the House of Terror Museum, a powerful and sobering look at Hungary's fascist and communist past.
day_by_day.evening: Take a Danube River cruise at sunset — a magical way to see the illuminated Parliament, Chain Bridge, Buda Castle, and bridges all lit up at night. Several operators offer 1-hour cruises (~€12-18).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast near the hotel before heading to the baths
meals.lunch: Bagolyvár Restaurant — a charming, affordable restaurant in City Park serving Hungarian home-style cooking (~€12-16)
meals.dinner: Borkonyha Winekitchen — a Michelin-starred restaurant offering excellent Hungarian cuisine with a focus on local wines at surprisingly reasonable prices for the quality (~€25-35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Széchenyi Baths entry ~€22-28 (includes locker). Bring a swimsuit, towel, and flip flops — or rent them there. The House of Terror Museum is emotionally intense but historically invaluable. Book the Danube cruise in advance in September.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Budapest — explore the charming Óbuda district (the oldest part of Budapest) or the Kiraly Street and Gozsdu Udvar courtyard area for local boutiques and café culture. Visit the Central Market Hall (Nagyvásárcsarnok) to pick up Hungarian souvenirs: paprika, pálinka (fruit brandy), Tokaji wine, and handmade crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time — if flying out, head to Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport (~30 min by shuttle or taxi). If you have time, take a final stroll along the Danube embankment and enjoy one last langos or kürtőskalács from a street vendor. Reflect on an incredible week in two of Europe's most beautiful capitals.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or final evening in Budapest. If staying, enjoy a farewell dinner in the Belváros (Inner City) area.

meals.breakfast: Két Szerecsen — a beloved Budapest institution for breakfast and brunch with great coffee and international options (~€8-12)
meals.lunch: Falafel Faloda — a popular, affordable falafel spot in the Jewish Quarter, perfect for a quick and delicious final lunch (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown (if staying for evening) — a sleek riverside restaurant with modern Hungarian cuisine and great Danube views (~€20-30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for airport transfer and check-in. The airport shuttle (miniBUD) costs ~€8-10 per person. The Great Market Hall closes at 3 PM on Saturdays and is closed Sundays — Monday/Tuesday morning is ideal for shopping.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Prague Václav Havel Airport at 22:30 via Flight UA. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) will whisk you to your hotel in the heart of Prague. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of Moravian sparkling wine at the hotel bar before retiring for the night.

meals.breakfast: On board or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On board or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night supper at the hotel bar or in-room dining — charcuterie board, Czech open-faced sandwiches (chlebíčky), and herbal tea

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority. Confirm hotel late check-in ahead of time. Luggage handling should be handled by the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a leisurely gourmet breakfast at the hotel. At 10:00, embark on a private guided walking tour of Prague's UNESCO-listed Old Town (Staré Město). Explore the Astronomical Clock (Orloj) on the hour, wander through Old Town Square, admire the Gothic Týn Cathedral, and stroll the Baroque lanes. Stop for a private rooftop viewpoint experience over the terracotta skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the iconic Charles Bridge (Karlův most) — lined with Baroque statues — into the Lesser Town (Malá Strana). Ascend to Prague Castle (Pražský hrad), the largest ancient castle complex in the world. Explore St. Vitus Cathedral, the Golden Lane, and the Old Royal Palace with your private guide. Enjoy panoramic views over the red-roofed city.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a celebrated fine-dining restaurant such as La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise (1 Michelin star) for a multi-course tasting menu rooted in historic Czech cuisine — expect dishes like venison, river trout, and heirloom vegetables paired with curated Czech wines. After dinner, take a short moonlit stroll across Charles Bridge.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate hotel breakfast — pastries, smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh juices, and Czech cold cuts
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Café Savoy in Malá Strana — Art Nouveau interiors, duck confit, and Bohemian desserts
meals.dinner: La Degustation Bohême Bourgeoise — 10-course tasting menu with wine pairing (reserve well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Book Prague Castle skip-the-line tickets in advance. Private guide highly recommended for context-rich storytelling. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Charles Bridge is best experienced early morning or evening to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-17 (Thursday) — Prague: Jewish Quarter, Art & Velvet Culture
day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, visit Josefov — Prague's historic Jewish Quarter — one of the best-preserved in Europe. Tour the Old Jewish Cemetery, the Pinkas Synagogue (a haunting Holocaust memorial), and the Spanish Synagogue with its stunning Moorish interior. A private guide adds deep historical context to this emotionally significant site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Decorative Arts or the DOX Centre for Contemporary Art for a taste of Prague's thriving modern cultural scene. Alternatively, explore the Mucha Museum dedicated to Art Nouveau master Alfons Mucha. In the late afternoon, treat yourself to a Czech spa ritual — book a private session at a luxury hotel spa featuring beer baths and herbal wraps, a uniquely Bohemian wellness experience.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a classical music performance at the Estates Theatre (Stavovské divadlo), where Mozart himself premiered Don Giovanni in 1787 — a profoundly historic cultural experience. Post-concert, enjoy cocktails at a sophisticated rooftop bar such as T-Anker or Cloud 9 with sweeping Old Town views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh Czech pastries and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lokál Dlouhááá — an upscale Czech gastropub with perfectly poured Pilsner Urquell and traditional svíčková (beef sirloin in cream sauce)
meals.dinner: Pre-theatre dinner at Bellevue Restaurant — elegant Continental and Czech cuisine with castle views over the Vltava River

day_by_day.notes: Book Estates Theatre tickets well in advance — performances sell out. Jewish Quarter entry requires a combined ticket — purchase online. The beer spa experience should be pre-booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-18 (Friday) — Prague to Budapest: The Grand Transfer
day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely breakfast in Prague. Spend the late morning doing any last-minute exploration — browse the Havelské Tržiště market for artisan souvenirs, Bohemian crystal, or local garnets. Pack and check out with full concierge luggage assistance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Prague for Budapest via a premium private transfer or first-class rail journey on the EuroCity train (approximately 7 hours, scenic Danube valley route) or a short 1-hour private charter flight. Arrive in Budapest in the late afternoon. Check in to your luxury Budapest accommodation — ideally a grand property along the Danube such as the Four Seasons Gresham Palace or Matild Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Orient yourself with a gentle evening stroll along the Danube Promenade (Duna-korzó) on the Pest side, taking in the illuminated Parliament Building, Chain Bridge, and Buda Castle reflected in the river. Enjoy a welcome cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the river.

meals.breakfast: Final grand hotel breakfast in Prague
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic or first-class dining car on the train — or a light meal at Budapest Keleti station upon arrival
meals.dinner: Costes Downtown or Onyx Restaurant (Michelin-starred Hungarian fine dining) — celebrate your arrival in Budapest with a tasting menu of elevated Magyar cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Private transfer Prague–Budapest costs approx. €400–600 and takes 4.5–5 hours. First-class train is scenic and comfortable. Book Budapest hotel well in advance — September is peak season. Hotel concierge in Budapest should be briefed on preferences before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: After a sumptuous hotel breakfast, cross the Chain Bridge (Széchenyi Lánchíd) and ascend Castle Hill via the historic Funicular (Budavári Sikló). Explore the magnificent Buda Castle complex — the Hungarian National Gallery, the medieval castle district, Matthias Church (Mátyás-templom) with its dazzling Zsolnay tile roof, and the Fishermen's Bastion (Halászbástya) offering some of the most breathtaking panoramic views in all of Europe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into the Pest side and visit the Hungarian Parliament Building — one of the grandest Neo-Gothic structures in the world. Book a premium guided interior tour to see the Holy Crown of Hungary. Afterward, explore the Great Market Hall (Nagycsarnok) for artisan Hungarian paprika, Tokaji wine, and handcrafted folk art.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in Budapest's legendary thermal bath culture — book a private evening session at the Széchenyi or Gellért Thermal Baths, or for ultimate luxury, reserve a private suite at the Veli Bej Bath. Dine afterward at a riverside restaurant with Parliament views.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast — Hungarian rétes (strudel), cold cuts, fresh langos, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Halászbástya Restaurant — elegant lunch at the Fishermen's Bastion with castle panorama views; try fogas (pike-perch) and Hungarian goulash
meals.dinner: Spoon The Boat — a floating fine-dining restaurant on the Danube with stunning Parliament views; contemporary Hungarian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Fishermen's Bastion is free to enter (tower access has a small fee). Parliament tours must be booked in advance. Private thermal bath sessions should be arranged through the hotel concierge. September evenings can be cool — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-20 (Sunday) — Budapest: Andrássy Avenue, Heroes & Ruin Bars
day_by_day.morning: Stroll the grand UNESCO-listed Andrássy Avenue — Budapest's answer to the Champs-Élysées — lined with Neo-Renaissance palaces, boutiques, and embassies. Visit the Hungarian State Opera House for a behind-the-scenes guided tour of its opulent gilded interior. Continue to Heroes' Square (Hősök tere) and the Millennial Monument — a powerful tribute to Hungarian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore City Park (Városliget) and visit Vajdahunyad Castle — a fairy-tale structure built for the 1896 Millennial Exhibition combining Romanesque, Gothic, and Baroque styles. Nearby, the Museum of Fine Arts houses an impressive European collection. In the late afternoon, visit the Great Synagogue on Dohány Street — the largest synagogue in Europe and a deeply moving cultural landmark.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Budapest's iconic ruin bar scene — but in style. Begin at Szimpla Kert (the original ruin bar) for the cultural experience, then move to a more refined cocktail bar such as High Note SkyBar (rooftop, panoramic views) or Boutiq'Bar for craft cocktails. End the night with a late supper of Hungarian street food — lángos, kürtőskalács, and chimney cake.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a visit to a classic Budapest café such as Gerbeaud Café on Vörösmarty Square — established 1858, famous for Dobos torte and espresso
meals.lunch: Borkonyha WineKitchen (Michelin-starred) — Hungarian wine-centric tasting menu with seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Late-night supper at Mák Bistro — intimate, creative Hungarian bistro cuisine with natural wines

day_by_day.notes: Opera House tours sell out — book online in advance. The Great Synagogue charges a modest entry fee and is closed on Saturdays (Jewish Sabbath) — Sunday is ideal. Ruin bars are lively on Sunday evenings. Dress smart-casual for fine dining.

day_by_day.date: 2027-09-21 (Monday) — Budapest: Danube Bend Day Trip & Culinary Immersion
day_by_day.morning: Embark on a private luxury day trip to the Danube Bend (Dunakanyar) — one of Central Europe's most scenic stretches of river. Visit the charming baroque town of Szentendre, known for its Serbian Orthodox churches, cobblestone streets, and thriving art galleries. Explore the Marzipan Museum and browse artisan studios.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Visegrád — a dramatic medieval hilltop citadel with sweeping views over the Danube — and Esztergom, Hungary's ancient capital, dominated by the massive Esztergom Basilica, the largest church in Hungary. Return to Budapest by private car in the late afternoon, refreshed and culturally enriched.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Hungarian State Opera House — book premium seats for an opera or ballet; the interior alone is worth the visit. Pre-performance champagne reception in the gilded foyer. Post-performance, a late dinner at a celebrated Budapest restaurant to close the evening in style.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch prepared by the hotel along the Danube Bend — local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh bread, and Tokaji Aszú dessert wine
meals.dinner: Costes Restaurant (first Michelin-starred restaurant in Hungary) — contemporary European tasting menu with Hungarian soul

day_by_day.notes: Private car for the Danube Bend excursion takes approximately 4–5 hours total. Book Opera tickets months in advance for September performances. The hotel concierge can arrange a gourmet picnic basket. Esztergom Basilica has a panoramic viewing gallery worth climbing.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a long, indulgent farewell breakfast at the hotel — savor every last bite of Hungarian pastries, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee. Spend the final morning at leisure — a gentle walk along the Danube embankment, last-minute luxury shopping on Váci Street or Andrássy Avenue (Hungarian porcelain from Herend, Tokaji wine, paprika sets), or a final soak at a thermal bath.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel with full concierge luggage assistance. Depart for Budapest Ferenc Liszt International Airport via private luxury transfer. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for a smooth, stress-free airport experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure flight. Carry beautiful memories of Prague's Gothic spires, Budapest's grand boulevards, thermal baths, Michelin-starred feasts, and the timeless flow of the Danube.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell hotel breakfast — the full spread
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Gerbeaud Café or a final bowl of authentic Hungarian gulyás at a classic étterem near the hotel
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer the night before. Confirm flight check-in requirements. Hungarian customs allow wine and spirits within EU duty-free limits — stock up on Tokaji Aszú as the perfect souvenir. Budapest Airport has a good duty-free selection for last-minute gifts.
